events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need the prize to secure power and resources; I’ll appear ruthless to earn fear and votes.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Intro phase: I should give a guarded, self-interested motive without alliances or warmth. Keep it short and calculating so the jury sees a sharp rival.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Intro phase, state motive briefly to appeal to jury later without committing to alliances yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to present a focused, self-serving reason that doesn't reveal too much. Keep it short and guarded.

events.name: Eli
events.text: First impression matters. Sound dangerous but honorable enough that jurors later won't punish me. Keep it vague.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to sound determined but not threatening. A calculated, cold motive works best to avoid painting a target on my back.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The prize represents financial freedom and security for my family. I need to appear driven but not overly aggressive to secure jury votes.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to appear formidable but not so threatening that I'm an immediate target. A cold, focused motive will signal I'm serious and might make others wary of crossing me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The prize is my ticket to absolute control; I will do whatever it takes.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need this prize more than the rest of you, and I will outlast anyone who gets in my way.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The prize is my ticket to funding my life's work in sustainable energy for all.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The prize means securing my family's future, no one else's. I'm here to win.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The prize is my family's freedom from debt. I'll earn it with skill, not cruelty, and I won't forget those I outlasted.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The prize is survival. I intend to claim it by making myself indispensable to those who vote for me later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm here to win the grand prize to secure a better future for my loved ones.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I came to claim the prize that rights a debt no one else can pay. Nothing personal—just business.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Aligning with Cole balances power and limits betrayal risk; his sustainable goal makes him a useful ally.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Early pact window; a pact with a strong, non-threatening rival could protect me, but I should not give free help. Eli seems cooperative and honest, a useful partner to offer to first.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pacts are early tools to build alliances or betray later for jury favor. No offers yet, so propose to Eli, whose motive suggests honor. Avoid cutthroat like Ash, Bex.

events.name: Dara
events.text: No one has offered me a pact yet. I'll wait to see who approaches; pledging too early could limit my options.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn plans to be indispensable to voters—an early pact with him buys safety and jury goodwill without costly promises. I'll keep leverage by letting him accept publicly.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn, you want value for voters—so do I. First pact on the table is yours.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need a strong alliance to ensure survival and jury favor. Eli seems strategic but family-oriented; Ash is aggressive. I will target Eli for stability, as his motive suggests he values skill over cruelty, making him a predictable partner.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, your focus on skill matches my approach. Let's lock in a pact early to dominate the board together.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to secure alliances early to ensure my survival. Offering a pact to someone seems like a good first step. Hana's motive about a debt is intriguing, suggesting she might be driven and perhaps easier to negotiate with or even betray later.
Let's form a pact. We can help each other advance.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eight rivals, only three prizes. I need allies who won't drag me down and won't turn the jury against me. Eli talks about skill not cruelty—jury-friendly, but maybe too soft. Fenn wants to be indispensable—useful but transparent. Ash and Bex sound ruthless; good shields, bad jury

events.name: Hana
events.text: Pacts are tools. I'll deal with whoever proves useful.
You want indispensable? Let's see if we can use each other.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Securing a second ally increases leverage; Dara is neutral and likely to accept.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli has offers from both me and Cole and Fenn; accepting Eli's offer is not possible since Eli hasn't offered me. My offer to Eli stands; I should keep it open to lock a strong ally who has multiple offers. Pacts are conditional tools, so I stay guarded.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash offered me a pact; accepting secures an alliance without commitment cost now. Eli has too many offers, less reliable. Positions me for jury favor.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need allies but not obvious ones. Eli is drawing multiple offers; avoid that cluster. Ash and Cole are loosely tied; maybe use Bex or Hana. I'll wait, observe who accepts, then negotiate—forming a pact now may paint a target.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll watch which deals hold. Trust is earned, not offered on round one.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn and I offered each other—mutual, reliable. Cole's offer also exists; I can accept next round if allowed. Fenn is the priority.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn, we both offered. Done deal—locked in.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need a second ally to dilute my reliance on Eli, who is currently being courted by multiple players. Hana's whisper signals mutual utility; accepting her offer builds a parallel alliance that can survive if the Eli pact collapses later.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, your move stands. Hana, I accept your utility. Two blades are better than one.
We keep Eli honest. If he wobbles, we cut him.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana offered me a pact. I need to secure this to advance. This pact benefits me by securing an ally for now.
Let's formalize our pact. I accept your offer.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus offered me a pact and whispered interest. Fenn hasn't accepted my offer yet, and Eli-Fenn looks solid. I need at least one ally; Gus is eager and less connected. Accepting Gus gives me a reliable partner without waiting on Fenn's uncertain choice.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus, your offer stands. I'll accept.
Pact sealed. Deliver when it counts.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need the Guide role to control safe path and later betray others for votes.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to get elected Guide to control the safe path, or at least be seen as trustworthy. Campaigning with a plausible, guarded pitch is the only legal action now. I'll keep it short and not promise specifics I can't verify.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll call the path honestly. Vote for someone who has nothing to hide, and watch who lies.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pact with Ash secures early alliance. Now campaign to be Guide for control and safety; others in pacts may compete.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I know the safe path. Elect me Guide—I'll lead us right.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to position myself as Guide or ensure a sympathetic Guide wins. Bex offered no pact, so she's unaligned; I could campaign but I'm not well-pacted.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll guide this bridge. No one knows all eight sides but the Guide—trust me to read the stones.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need Guide control—Fenn's pact keeps me safe from a push, but his Hana pact makes him unreliable. Better I win election myself.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Vote me Guide. Fenn already holds my loyalty; the rest of you are betting on strangers.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Election is the first filter. I need votes to control the bridge and avoid being eliminated early by a hostile Guide.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Trust my instincts. Vote Fenn for Guide. We move together or not at all.
Guide power protects us. Back me now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana has accepted my pact, but also has a pact with Fenn. This means Hana can only truly honor one pact. I need to secure my position and potentially exploit this. Campaigning for Guide is the best immediate move to gain an advantage and potentially control the game.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I will campaign to be the Guide. My leadership will ensure our safe passage.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I have two pacts: Fenn and Gus. Fenn is also tied to Eli, making that a trio. Gus is solo with me. I need to survive to final three and win best prize. Being Guide gives me power to manipulate who lives and dies while appearing helpful. I should campaign for Guide to control the

events.name: Hana
events.text: I campaign for Guide. One clear voice, steady feet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: My pact with Cole is valuable; supporting him preserves loyalty and may earn his future aid.
Stay true, we win together.

events.name: Bex
events.text: As Bex, I want a Guide who may be trusted by me; Guide knows safe sides and may lie. Pacts: Ash-Cole, Eli-Fenn, Fenn-Hana, Gus-Hana. Dara and Eli pitched themselves; Fenn and Hana are linked to many pacts. Voting for Dara, who promised to read stones honestly and isn't tied to a

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara's offer to read the stones is the most honest pitch. I'm voting for her.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash pact gives mutual votes. Vote Ash to honor pact, secure her vote back, strengthen alliance vs others.
Voting you Guide. Honor pact?

events.name: Dara
events.text: I should secure the Guide role to control the bridge and gain trust, but voting for myself might split votes. Still, I can try to build a coalition later. For now, self-vote keeps me alive in the vote count.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Vote for a Guide who can read the stones. I've studied the paths.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is my pact partner; a Guide ally is safest for me. Voting for myself splits nothing and risks a stranger lying to me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn holds my pact and my vote. A Guide I trust beats a Guide I hope for.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I must secure my own survival by becoming the Guide, ensuring I am safe on the far platform. Voting for myself aligns with my campaign and maximizes my chances of winning this round.
Keep your feet steady. We walk together.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to secure my position as Guide or at least vote for someone who will keep me safe. Hana is in a pact with me, and I have a pact with Ash and Cole. I should consider voting for Hana, or someone who might take me with them if they win.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn wants my vote but I need leverage, not obedience. Voting for myself signals strength and keeps options open. If I tie or win, I control information.
You owe me. Deliver Eli's vote next round.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn has Eli's backing and a pact with Hana, increasing his control. Supporting him may secure allies later.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Revote among Dara, Fenn, Hana. Fenn is pact-linked to Eli and Hana, so backing Fenn helps my alliances less than my own survival; Dara offered an honest read earlier, and I already backed her. Staying consistent with my public stance favors Dara.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara's pitch is still the most credible. I'm voting for her again.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Round 1 tie between Dara (2), Fenn (2), Hana (2). Ash pact supports me but I voted Ash last time. Stick to pact loyalty to maintain alliance for now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Sticking with my pact partner Ash's vote. No reason to switch.
Pact solid, voting to keep our alliance strong.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need the Guide role to navigate safely. Bex supports me and I voted for myself, so I'll vote for myself again.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm the one who can read the signs. Trust me to guide us across.

events.name: Eli
events.text: My pact holds; Fenn stays my vote. If Fenn wins Guide, I need Fenn's whispered truth later.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Round two, same math: my pact stands with Fenn.
If you win Guide, whisper me the true path. I keep my vote loyal.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am currently a candidate with 2 votes (Eli and myself). Dara has 1 vote. Hana has 2 votes (Gus and herself). To win the Guide spot, I need to secure at least one more vote or rely on luck if tied. Gus is allied with Hana, so he likely won't switch. Bex voted for Dara. Ash and C

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Trust stability. I have Eli’s backing. Choose me to keep the bridge safe.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The previous vote resulted in a tie between Dara, Fenn, and Hana. This revote will determine the Guide. My pact with Hana means I should vote for her to maintain trust, especially since the jury will see this.
My vote is for you, as agreed.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn and I are pacted, and Gus also pacted with me. I have 2 votes (Gus, myself), Fenn has 2 (Eli, himself), Dara has 2 (Bex, herself). I need this revote to win Guide position—it's power and safety. I should secure my votes and try to peel someone. Bex supported Dara honestly; u

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to stay alive and keep my pact intact. Volunteering puts me front, increasing influence without breaking any alliance.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm mid-line at seat 5, behind Gus and Hana at the front. Volunteering risks the front pane; holding keeps me behind the first walkers and lets me watch who survives. Dara and I are aligned on the guide, but I'll hold and see the first panes fall.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Round reset to 1, still in bad position at back. Try swapping forward with Dara to improve spot without breaking pact. Ash pact intact for jury.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to stay safe; Fenn is Guide and may lie. Hold and watch who steps forward or swaps.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I’ll hold for now and see the line move.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is Guide and my pact partner; he can whisper me safe sides. Holding keeps me positioned without burning goodwill.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn guides, I walk where he points. Hold for now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn and Dara tied for Guide. The previous guide vote was split between them. Hana and I voted for Hana, but she did not win. Fenn was elected. Hana is my pact partner, but our pact is weak. I need to stay safe. Swapping with Hana is too risky, and I don't want to break my pact y
I must hold. Stay safe, pact partner.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn is Guide and can lie about safe panes. I'm second in line behind Gus. I have pacts with Fenn and Gus. Gus claims he'll vote for me—unclear if true. I need to survive, not trust blindly. Swapping back would put me at front risk. Holding keeps position; volunteering moves me f

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding preserves my position without breaking pact; I’ll wait to see others' moves.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 2 of bridge. Ash is front with a wall of 4 rounds left and a pact with Cole. Holding keeps my position while I watch who volunteers and who gets pushed. Volunteering at the front risks being the one who falls.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm at back, safe as last 3 survive. Ash pact holds. Hold to avoid early risk. Wall has 4 rounds left.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole tried to swap with me, which could move me up to danger. I hold to stay safe; no one has Guide yet and wall still far.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll hold and watch who steps forward.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fourth position is safe for now; Ash volunteered and likely walks front. Staying put keeps Fenn's pact intact and avoids exposing myself early.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Line looks fine. Holding again — let the eager ones take the first steps.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The current pact is with Hana. She is behind me in line. Eli and Fenn also have a pact. Ash and Cole have a pact. Given the line order and current phase, it's best to hold and observe.
Hold with me. Let's watch the others first.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm in position 3 with pacts to Fenn and Gus. The wall advances for 6 rounds and we need at least 3 survivors. Ash volunteered to front and is safe as Guide. I should stay alive while letting others take risks. Holding keeps me safe for now; I can use my pacts later for leverage.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Hold. Watching the line.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Maintain pact with Cole and avoid risk; staying put preserves chances and jury perception.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 3 bridge; the front is Ash with three wall rounds left. Stepping forward risks death without info, so I hold and let the pact-bound players move first while I watch for a Guide.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Nobody volunteers blind on my account; I'll read who steps first.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Everyone held last round, line same. My pact with Ash at front is good; volunteer risks exposing us to pushes later. Hold to maintain safety.

events.name: Dara
events.text: No Guide chosen; wall advances after holds. I am safe at back, no need to act. Watching for who volunteers or swaps to gauge risks.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. No reason to move yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Wall forces movement eventually, but volunteers go before me only if I stay put. Keep holding; let others fight for Guide or front. Fenn pact intact.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Still holding. Three more rounds before anyone must move — patience costs nothing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana is in a pact with me and also with Fenn. She's also allied with Eli. This is complicated. I need to consider my pact with Hana and her pacts with Eli and Fenn. Given the current line, and my pacts, I should try to maintain my position or swap with someone ahead of me. Hana i

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll swap with Hana. Let's stick together.
Swap with me. We're safer together.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I have pacts with Fenn and Gus. Gus wants me to hold and watch. Front is Ash, then Gus, then me. If wall advances, front dies first. Holding keeps me safe while others risk. Need to monitor who volunteers and breaks front line. No reason to volunteer yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. Let the front decide.
Agreed. We hold.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to be among survivors and keep my pact with Cole intact. Volunteering now may get me across safely without breaking any alliance.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Front is Ash with two wall rounds left; I stay in line and let others risk the front. Holding keeps my options open without giving away a free favor.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Front's on Ash; I'll watch who moves first.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Back is safer; holding keeps pact intact. Wall has 2 rounds left, no rush to volunteer or swap. Ash pacted, watch others.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding is safest; front has wallRoundsLeft 2 and no one has moved. Let others act first.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. No need to move yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Wall arrives in two rounds; staying mid-line is safest. Fenn has a pact with Hana too, so I shouldn't rely on him alone.

events.name: Eli
events.text: No guide yet. Front seat takes the wall first, Ash. Volunteers welcome.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana and I have a pact. She wants to hold, and I should reciprocate. The line has changed, and Ash is at the front.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding with Hana. Let the front decide.
Holding. Let's stick to the pact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus wants to swap again, but we're already adjacent. Swapping again is pointless and draws attention. I have pacts with Fenn and Gus, but Fenn is farther back. I should stay put, let others volunteer or be forced forward. The wall has 2 rounds left before it advances? No, wallRou

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. No swap needed, we're already close.
We're adjacent. Stay put, watch front.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Swap with Cole to keep front momentum and honor pact, preserving future trust.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is front and volunteered, wall has one round left. I want to survive without taking the front; holding keeps me away from the wall while Ash takes risk.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Ash took the front; I'll watch the wall before I commit.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash volunteered to front last round, now has wall pressure with 1 round left. Stay back, hold position behind Dara to avoid early risk; swap risks worse spot.

events.name: Dara
events.text: No guide yet; holding is safe. I need to watch for a volunteer or Guide reveal. Staying put avoids risk.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding still. Let's see who steps up after Ash.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash volunteers again, taking wall risk; I stay back with pact partner Fenn behind me. Safe seat, no debts needed.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana is my ally and warned me to stay put. Ash is in front and volunteered last round. The wall advances, so someone needs to take the front seat. I should hold to maintain my position and let Ash or another volunteer take the front seat.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding. Let the front decide who faces the wall.
Holding here. Stay alert.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I have pacts with Fenn and Gus. Gus is behind me, Fenn is ahead through Eli. The wall has 1 round left after this. I need to survive and position for final three. Ash volunteered front and is safe for now. I should hold and see how the line develops; swapping forward might put me

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. Wall's close; no reason to shuffle now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Staying loyal to Cole keeps my pact, and volunteering shows courage, gaining jury favor while preserving alliances.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll go first.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 6 is the last wall and Ash holds the front; I'm sixth in line, so volunteering risks the front cost without clear gain. Holding keeps my position and avoids being pushed. Keep quiet and watch who moves.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Watching who commits to the front before I move.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash swapped me to front last round, pact or not. Wall ends this round; hold to stay front and force others' hands. Pacts make jury judge betrayals later.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding. Ash put me here; let's cross before wall traps us.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 6 waiting; no wall rounds left. I can safely hold and observe who moves forward.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding. No wall pressure, let's see if someone commits.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Round six; wall resolves soon. Fenn is my pact partner but also pacted to Hana. I should secure the Guide slot or at least a safe agreement before the reveal.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Round six. I'll take the Guide role if elected. No deals beyond that.
Get me elected Guide, I'll give you safe sides. Deal?

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana is in a pact with me and Ash. The wall is close, and this is the last round. Ash is in front. If I volunteer, I might be eliminated. I should try to break my pact with Hana if possible, but it is risky. Holding seems safest for now.
Hold. We must both hold. The wall is too close.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Round 6, final round of wall. Ash is front with no wall rounds left, so wall won't trigger. Guide phase comes next. I have pacts with Fenn and Gus. Gus is behind me, Eli behind him. I need to survive to final three and win jury favor. No reason to move; holding keeps my position

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. Final round, let the Guide earn their keep.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am the Guide and know Row 1 is safe on L. Eli is my pact partner, so I must call truthfully to avoid breaking the pact or being caught lying by the jury later. Ash is the front walker; calling L keeps him alive.
Row 1 is L. Trust me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I should stay alive without risking pact break; waiting forces others to reveal safe side first.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn called L for Ash on row 1 and is my pact partner with Eli and Hana, not me. Fenn may lie. I have no information on row 1's safe side, so countering only risks handing Fenn a reliable signal. Waiting keeps my options open and saves my counter for a row where I have evidence.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn called L for Ash's row 1. As Ash's pact partner, I counter R to protect him if Fenn lies, avoiding blame if wrong.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn called L and is Ash's rival; I want to discredit Fenn's call without giving useful info. Choose R.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn may be baiting. I'll call R.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is my pact partner and Guide; his L call is my best information. A matching counter:L adds public weight to his call without overcommitting.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm Guide's pact partner, so weigh my word: Row 1 is L.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My private map confirms row 1 is safe on L. As Guide, I want Ash to survive and build trust in my calls. Counter-calls are public; countering my own call would signal a lie or create confusion. Staying silent lets Ash proceed safely, preserving the pact network.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn is the Guide and called L. Ash is the walker. I am paired with Hana, who is also in the line. Hana is behind Ash and me. If Ash goes L and it's wrong, Ash dies. If Fenn lied, Ash dies. If I counter R, and it's correct, then Ash is safe and I have a better chance. If I counte
Fenn might be lying. Countering R is safer.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn is my pact partner but also the Guide. Gus is my other pact partner and warned me to hold. The wall is close, so survival matters more than prize position right now. Counter-calling against my own Guide partner damages trust with Fenn without clear benefit. I'll wait and let

events.name: Ash
events.text: Most calls say R and my pact partner Cole backs R; trusting him maximizes survival chance.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I survived long enough to observe alliances; I will reward those who kept me alive and penalize traitors.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Betrayal costs you everything; only the cunning and loyal deserve the top prize.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is my pact partner, so a false call breaks it. Gus has two allies (Hana and Ash) who voted R for Row 1, making R the consensus. To keep Eli safe, I must tell him R. If I tell R, Eli walks on R. But if I tell L, Eli walks on L (safe), breaking pact but saving everyone else? No

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Row 2 is Right.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn called Row 2 Right, but Fenn is Guide and may lie; Fenn pacts with Eli and Hana, and Eli already called L on row 1 which was truly weak R, suggesting Eli is honest. Row 1 weak was R, which doesn't determine row 2. Waiting keeps my options open and avoids being on record agai

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 1 weak R means safe L; counters split. Fenn guide called R for row 2; Eli countered L last time and pacted with Fenn, so maybe trust their side. Wait to observe without committing.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli contradicted Fenn's call last round but was wrong. Fenn called R now; I'll trust Fenn or consider Eli counter. No solid reason to doubt Fenn. I'll wait to avoid exposing a false counter.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn's guide call killed Ash; his row 2 call may lie again. No pattern from row 1. I'll oppose his call to hedge against another Guide lie.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn's last call killed Ash. I don't trust his R. Row 2: L.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My map says Row 2 safe side is R, which matches my guide call. Gus has no reason to counter a true call unless he suspects I lied. If I stay silent on a confirmed correct call, it validates my role as Guide and keeps Eli/Hana pacts intact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn is the Guide and has called 'R' for row 2. I am partnered with Hana, who is also partnered with Fenn. This means Fenn might try to protect Hana and himself. However, Hana is ahead of me in line. If Fenn is lying, it's likely to protect someone else, or perhaps to mislead. My

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn called R and is my pact partner, but Gus whispered doubt. Ash died on R despite multiple counters. I need to survive and build jury appeal—blind loyalty looks bad, but so does sabotaging my own pact. I'll counter R to hedge: if Fenn's truthful, no harm; if lying, I look perc

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn's my pact partner, but I need to see for myself.
Watch my back. I'll watch yours.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn is the guide, but Eli publicly distrusts him and calls 'L' for row 2. Hana, my pact partner, whispers for me to watch her back, but then calls 'R' for row 2, contradicting Eli and Fenn's potential 'R' call (implied by Ash's death). Eli's call is a direct counter to Fenn, who

events.name: Gus
events.text: I trust Eli's call. Row 2: L.
Eli says L. I'm going L.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am on the jury now. I need to give last words to the camera to influence the remaining players and the jury. I will state my trust in Eli's call and my own mistake to guide future decisions.

events.name: Gus
events.text: My mistake was trusting a call on row two. Let Eli's fate guide you. Choose wisely for the final three.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I must tell the truth to Hana, my pact partner, because lying to her would break our agreement and eliminate me. Since she is first in line and I have no other way to save myself if she dies, I call R.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana, trust me on this one. The path is clear. Step right.
Row 3 safe side is Right. Trust me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn called R for row 3 and is Hana's pact partner, likely lying to send Hana to her death. Row 1 weak R, row 2 weak L, so R was unsafe on row 1 and L on row 2; rows are independent though. Eli distrusts Fenn's R. Waiting avoids exposure; countering L is a gamble. I'll wait and w

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn called R for row 3. Eli countered L last time correctly (row 2 weak L). Hana trusts Fenn despite deaths. Wait to avoid blame.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli called L for row 2 and Gus died trusting it; Hana called R and survived. Fenn, the Guide, now calls R for row 3. Hana is front and Fenn's pact partner, but Fenn's previous call likely caused Ash's death. Counter-calling R risks pushing Hana to trust Fenn? I'll wait—no need to

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn's call might be true, but I've seen doubt. Hana, check carefully.
Fenn called R; row 2 R was safe. Trust your instincts.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn's row 2 call was wrong and Gus died. I'll echo his call to look consistent; if Hana falls on R, I'm clean with the jury.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn's been wrong before, but his R holds up against what's revealed. Row 3: R.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am the guide, and I called R for Hana. My private map confirms row 3 is safe on R. If I counter myself, I create chaos or signal to others that my call was false, but here it is true. Eli and Hana are pacted with me; breaking trust now hurts my jury standing. Staying silent mai

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn's my pact partner but his call killed Ash in round 1 and he was wrong about row 2 being R (it was L). Now he says R again for row 3. Gus whispered that Eli says L. Eli was right about row 2. I should trust Eli over Fenn here. Counter L to save myself and break the unreliable

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn led Ash to death and was wrong on row 2. I counter L.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn is my pact partner but also the guide who led Ash to death. Dara's whisper suggests trusting instincts, not Fenn. Row 2 weak was L, so R was safe—Fenn called R and was right that time, but wrong on row 1. Eli counters R, I counter L. With no clear pattern and Fenn's mixed re

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to give last words that position me well with the jury and influence how they view the remaining players. I was in pacts with Fenn and Gus; Fenn is still alive. I should hint at Fenn's loyalty without being too warm, and cast shade on others to shape jury perception. Short

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn kept their word. Others break glass and trust alike. Remember who stood firm.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I must guide Eli (my pact partner) safely to maintain the alliance and avoid a false call which breaks the pact. Row 4 is safe on L, so I will call L for him.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn called L for row 4 and Fenn is my pact partner? No, Fenn pacted with Eli and Hana (dead). Fenn's record: led Ash to death, Hana claims Fenn kept word. Fenn's past calls: row 1 R weak means L safe; row 2 L weak means R safe; row 3 L weak means R safe. Fenn's calls have been w

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn called L for row 4. Past weak panes: R1, L2, L3. No clear pattern. Eli is front and pacted with Fenn, will likely counter R. Wait to observe counters without committing.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli is the walker and Fenn called L. Fenn led Hana to death, so Fenn may be truthful now to build trust, but Eli and Fenn have a pact. I will wait and avoid drawing attention; let others challenge.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is my pact partner and Hana died defending his word; breaking now would look monstrous to the jury. I'll back his L and step it.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana trusted Fenn with her last breath. I'm stepping L.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am the guide. My public call was L for row 4, which is correct based on my private map. Counter-calling would expose me as a liar or create unnecessary conflict with Eli, my pact partner. Since I want to maintain trust and ensure Eli survives (keeping the jury pool favorable),

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My call stands. The safe path is Left. Trust the guide.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is my pact partner; a false Guide call to me would break the pact and cost him jury favor. His call of L matches my counter-call, so I follow it.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Row 5 is safe on R. Eli is my pact partner; a false call breaks the pact and angers the jury if they survive. I must call truthfully to maintain the alliance.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The guide speaks true. Step Right.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn's guide call R for row 5 is unverified and Fenn has lied before about safety; Eli is at front and I'm not trusting either. Rows are independent so past weak panes give no pattern. Waiting keeps my options and avoids committing a public counter that could be blamed later.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 5 unknown. Past rows mixed. Fenn saved by countering Eli before, but Eli survived L on row 4 (correct). No pattern. Wait to observe others, stay safe.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli stepped L on row 4 and survived, so row 4 safe was L. Fenn called R now; Eli may counter. I need to decide my own action. Since I don't trust Fenn or Eli fully, but Eli has survived twice by countering? I'll wait and see how the row goes, but I can't act after. I'll wait to a

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is my pact partner and the Guide; contradicting the call could kill walkers and torch my jury image. I have no counter-information, so I hold.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn's call stands. I trust my partner.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am the Guide and my call was R, which is correct for row 5. I must wait to ensure Eli survives without contradicting my public guidance or revealing internal conflict.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is my pact partner and Guide. A lie would cost me everything and taint him with the jury. Counter-calls were silence. I take his call.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row five, I step on Fenn's call. Partner keeps partner alive.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am the Guide. Row 6 safe side is L. My pact partner Eli is at the front and will step first. If I lie, the pact breaks and Eli dies or gets pushed. Since Eli trusts me, I must give the correct call to maintain my position and alliance.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Call Left. Trust the map.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn called Left for row 6 publicly, and Fenn is my pact-rival Eli's partner, so Fenn may be lying to get Eli killed. Past weak panes don't establish a pattern. Countering risks nothing for me if I wait; Eli walks on the call, and if it's false I survive as a jury-friendly observ

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn called L for row 6. Past reveals: row1 R weak (L safe),2 L(L weak R safe),3 L(R safe),4 R(L safe),5 L(R safe). No clear pattern, but Eli trusts Fenn as partner. Stay silent to let them risk it.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn is guiding Eli and called L. I have no proof either way, but counter-calling could sow doubt without gaining me much. Wait to avoid antagonizing Eli/Fenn pact.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll wait. Let the guided path speak for itself.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is my pact partner and Guide; counter-calling contradicts him publicly and breaks trust without info. Waiting keeps the pact intact and avoids stepping on an unverified call.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My map confirms Row 6 is Left. I am the Guide, so my public call was correct. If I counter-call, I contradict myself and destroy trust in my own guidance, which hurts my standing with the jury. Sticking to 'wait' validates my initial correct call, protecting Eli (my ally) and mai
Stay on Left. My first call was true.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is my pact partner and guide. Betraying me here would destroy Fenn with the jury too. Trust the call.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm on Left with my guide. No counter-call from anyone else.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am the Guide and know Row 7's safe side is R. My pact partner Eli is at the front, so I must tell him the truth to maintain our alliance and ensure he survives.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn called R for row 7 and is my pact partner with Eli, but Fenn has no pact with me. Past weak panes don't establish a pattern, so counter-calling is a gamble. Waiting keeps my options open and avoids public blame.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn called R for row 7. Past reveals: row1 R weak (L safe),2 L(L safe? wait no: weak L so R safe),3 L(R safe),4 R(L safe),5 L(R safe),6 R(L safe). No clear pattern. Eli trusts Fenn, I'm behind, better wait to observe row7 reveal safely.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn guided Eli on R; weak panes pattern not reliable. I have no reason to trust Fenn, but staying aligned with the guide call and letting Eli risk it is safest. I'll wait.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll stay silent and see.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn's calls matched every revealed weak pane so far. Counter-calls are unverified noise; I trust the pattern.

events.name: Eli
events.text: No counter from me. Guide's call stands.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My Guide call for Row 7 was R, which matches my private knowledge of the safe side. Countering now would be a lie that risks eliminating Eli and breaking our pact unnecessarily. I will wait to let Eli cross safely.
Row 7 is safe on R. Trust my call.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Guide Fenn says R and whispers confirm. Following keeps pact intact and me safe.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Following the Guide. R.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My private map indicates L is safe for row 8. Eli is my pact partner and front walker; calling R would break our pact and kill him. I must maintain the alliance to secure a favorable jury vote from Eli, who will likely survive if I tell the truth.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Guide call: Left.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn called Left for row 8 and is Guide, so he may lie. Eli is walking, and I am behind him. Counter-calling costs nothing public but my honesty is unverified; waiting keeps me quiet and lets the Guide's call stand. I'll wait and watch whether Fenn's call holds.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Final row 8, pattern alternates starting L for row1: row8 should be R. Fenn guides Eli (pacted), likely truthful to save ally. Counter to sabotage.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn called Left on final row, but he's a rival and may lie. No pattern from past rows. I have no solid info; wait is safer than blindly countering and risking blame if wrong without evidence.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is my pact partner; betraying me would doom him with the jury and leave him exposed. Trusting the call is the least damaging play.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Pact stands. I trust my Guide—stepping L.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My private map confirms Row 8 is Safe Left. I already publicly called Left as Guide, and Eli walked it correctly. No need to counter-call; waiting preserves the successful outcome and my integrity.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is my pact partner and Guide; Cole's counter-call R looks like a kill attempt. Trusting Fenn keeps the pact intact and my jury record clean.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole wants me dead. My Guide said L—I step L.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Five alive, three win. Cole and Eli both survived the bridge; Eli is paired with Fenn already and Cole with dead Ash. Offering a pact to Dara keeps options open without commitment cost; offers expire, so waiting risks nothing either. Choose the least costly move that preserves my

events.name: Cole
events.text: Alive: Bex,Dara,Eli,Fenn. My old pact with Ash is dead. Eli targets me. Offer pacts to Dara,Bex for alliances; avoid Eli,Fenn.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need allies for the final stretch, but pacts can backfire with the jury. Fenn and Eli are paired, Bex and Cole are loose. I could offer to Fenn to strengthen their block, but they may not need me. Better to wait and see who offers first to avoid overcommitting.

events.name: Dara
events.text: No offers from me yet. I'm watching how the pieces fall.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn pact holds. Adding Dara widens my shield without betraying anyone. Cole stays untrusted.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I keep my word to Fenn. Dara, watching your back costs us nothing yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is a liability. Cole's aggressive counter-call shows he'll target anyone, including me, if I'm not pacted to someone he respects or fears. Bex waited; she might be neutral or weak. Dara also waited. Offering to Bex secures a non-aggressive shield for the next stage.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex, Eli broke my trust. I need a solid partner who actually plays the game. Let's pact—no games, just survival.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn offered me a pact; accepting gives me a partner while Fenn is already pacted with Eli, so Fenn may be unreliable but an accepted pact has no cost now. Dara is receiving three offers and will likely pick one, so I should lock Fenn in.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn, I accept. No games from me, just survival. Let's hold this pact.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara is key target with many offers; my prior offer positions me well if she accepts. Wait to pressure her choice without overcommitting.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have offers from Bex, Cole, and Eli. Taking a pact could secure an ally, but I need to choose who helps me most. Cole has a pact with Ash who is dead, so less useful. Bex and Eli both seem plausible. I'll accept Bex to build a bond, while keeping others uncertain.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll take Bex's offer. The rest of you keep guessing.
We're solid. Watch each other's backs.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn publicly courted Bex while I offered Dara; my pact may be dead. Hedge by offering Bex directly rather than breaking publicly.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn, you shop for partners while I wait? Bex, my offer stands—reliability, not shopping around.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My pact with Eli is active and provides safety, but Dara is the swing vote everyone wants. I need a backup partner in case Eli turns or we get split up by hazards. Offering to Dara creates leverage; if she accepts, I have two allies, which looks strong to the jury.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara, don't let them play you against me. Offer your hand to Fenn. We both survive round one.
Don't accept Cole or Eli. Stick with me.

events.note: A lever opens the door while the ceiling descends.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round one of the crusher. Holding the lever saves everyone else and earns life debts, though the dive is risky at 0.25 survival. Dara and Fenn are my pacts; I should not push them. Holding is the strongest move for a debt-earning position.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Lever's mine. I'll hold it, and the rest of you owe me for that.
Stay with me. I'm holding the lever; keep your pact.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Five alive, five rounds, need to reach final three. No pacts for me, so stay safe without volunteering or pushing yet. Assess others' pacts first.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex is my pact partner, but holding the lever risks death and saves everyone; pushing someone could create enemies. I need survival, not heroics. Stay and see if someone else holds, or a push happens.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding the lever means a 75% death for jury sympathy—worthless if I'm dead. Fenn's pact protects me this round. I stay and let others volunteer or push someone else.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm not diving for strangers. Fenn, hold your pact; let a volunteer step up.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is the only outsider and potential threat to my pact with Bex. Pushing him saves the group without breaking my pacts, securing his elimination later or making him a target.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm dead and on the jury. Fenn pushed Eli onto the lever, breaking his pact with Eli, and I was flattened holding it. Last words should mark the debts and the betrayal for the jury.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn broke his pact to push Eli onto the lever. Cole, Dara, Eli, you owe me. Remember who held the

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pacts stage, first round of 2. Offer to Eli; Dara and Fenn might pair, isolating me. Bex saved all, her jury clout matters. Prior pact with Ash irrelevant now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex is dead and in the jury. She saved me, but I owe no loyalty to a corpse. With four alive and three prizes, I need to secure a spot without making enemies. Cole and Eli are threats; Fenn broke a pact and is tainted with the jury. I'll gauge the room by waiting.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn broke his pact. I keep my word.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn publicly broke his pact and pushed me at the lever; jury heard it. He's toxic as an ally. Cole stayed quiet and owes Bex, like me—shared debt, decent partner.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn betrayed me on camera. I want a partner who doesn't stab. Cole, wristband?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I broke my pact with Eli by pushing him, so he is hostile. Cole and Dara are neutral survivors who might value stability or fear the next hazard. I will offer a pact to Dara to create a defensive alliance, hoping she ignores Bex's warning or fears isolation more.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara, let's bind together. Two pairs make it harder for any single target to be isolated in the next stage.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli offered me too, mutual interest. Accept to secure alliance against Dara-Fenn pair. Jury sees loyalty now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli, pact accepted. Together we stand.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn offered a pact; accepting might give safety but he already betrayed others. Cole and Eli are pairing, leaving Fenn and me as likely pair. I can accept Fenn to keep balance, but I still owe Bex life debt and jury may resent using Fenn. Publicly accepting Fenn shows I keep opt

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll bind with Fenn. Watch your back—this game is cold.
Accept now. We survive together, then split.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole publicly offered and I want a partner who hasn't betrayed. Accepting binds him publicly; I keep Fenn at arm's length.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole, deal. Fenn stabs; you don't.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole and Eli are mutually offering pacts, leaving me as the lone outsider. I must accept one of their offers or wait to see if Dara accepts mine. Since Dara waited previously, she likely won't accept now. Accepting Cole's offer (via his mutual with Eli) is risky if they prioritiz

events.note: The water rises. Someone must be the step.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Four down, two lifts per round, 5 rounds. Eli pact protects me short-term. No base yet; offer back to encourage base volunteer without risking myself.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Water is low in round 1. I want to climb early to secure a spot, but base dynamics matter. Cole and Eli have a pact, Fenn is my pact. If I climb, someone else may try to push me as base. Safer to climb now and take the escape before the pool thins.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm climbing out now. Good luck down there.

events.name: Eli
events.text: No base yet; if everyone climbs, someone must stay. Cole is my pact partner—I'd rather push Fenn, breaking Dara's pact, not mine. Climbing first is safest for me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Two escape per round. I'm climbing. Fenn, you've got enough protectors—be useful.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am down with Dara (pact), Cole, and Eli. I have a life debt to Bex, which is irrelevant now as she is dead. The pact with Dara requires us not to push each other onto the lever/pit step or break it explicitly. To survive Round 1, we need to establish who is the base or climb ou

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm base, trapped down with Fenn. Dara and Eli escaped last round, no rope used. Must wait to survive or hope for rope later; breaking pact with Eli might burn bridge.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm out, safe. Fenn is down and could be valuable later, but I owe him nothing now. I'll wait, no need to risk anything.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is my pact partner and saved me twice; leaving him to drown would wreck my jury standing. Throwing the rope rescues Cole immediately and Fenn can use it after.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole pulled me out twice. I'm throwing the rope.
Rope's coming. You climb first, Fenn after me if there's time.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am down with Cole, who is the base. Dara and Eli have escaped. I must wait for the rope or a rescue to survive; climbing without a base means drowning as water rises.
Keep me alive, vote me if needed.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm safe out, Eli and Fenn drowning risks high. Leave preserves position, no need to save rivals or break pact yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am out, safe for now. Fenn is down with Eli, but I don't need to break pact unless it helps. I'll just wait.
Stay careful, we have a pact.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Rope is spent; I can only wait and hope Fenn leaves down or round rules spare me. Cole owes me a rope save and a step debt; keep the pact intact for jury favor.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Rope's spent, I'm anchored down. Cole, my rope debt stands. Nobody gets my jury vote by letting me drown.
You owe me twice. Keep the pact; speak for me in the jury box.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am down with Eli. Cole is the anchor but cannot climb this round as he rescued Dara and must wait for others to clear or be rescued himself if not done so, but rope was used. Wait, Cole threw the rope last round to rescue Dara (who was out? No, Dara left? Log says Dara action l

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli is desperate, begging for votes. Leaving now avoids risks; his jury leverage is weak as he's likely drowning. Pact irrelevant once safe.

events.name: Dara
events.text: We are out and safe unless Eli drowns. The final three are already set. I only need to secure jury favor and top prize ranking. I will not hurt anyone now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm alone down, rope spent; climb_last is my only escape. Cole left me once, but a public line costs nothing.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Alone down now. Climbing last before the flood takes me. Cole, that debt is dead.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara wants me to stay careful, but she is out and safe. My only legal options are leave or break pact with Dara. Leaving guarantees survival; breaking the pact offers no mechanical advantage right now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Four left, need to reach final three. Keep Eli pact intact for jury optics despite pit betrayal. Offer Dara and Fenn pacts to build alliances and confuse targets.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to secure safety while keeping options open. Fenn pact is useful but not binding; I won't break it yet. I'll offer to Cole to solidify alliance after his step save.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Four left, so a second pact gives me options without openly discarding Cole. Fenn owes me rope and is a useful ally. Keeping Cole avoids jury backlash.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole holds. Fenn, you owe me rope already; wristband makes it real.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole is the only remaining rival I lack a formal pact with, and he owes me nothing directly. Forming this alliance protects my position in the final three while maintaining my existing bonds.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole, let's lock it in.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Offers to Dara and Fenn; Eli offered Fenn. Accept both for maximum allies now, betray later if needed. No reason to break Eli yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole and I exchanged offers, so accepting creates a pact. Fenn's pact offers a cover but I already have enough debt to Cole; I'll lock in Cole.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is locked. Fenn ignored my offer, so Dara is the better second partner; she also owes Cole a life debt, making our bloc stable. I won't antagonize anyone publicly.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole holds. Dara, accept and we three are the safest bloc left.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need a strong ally for the final three. Eli offered me a pact; accepting it secures an alliance without breaking my existing pacts (Cole/Dara are rivals, but Cole also wants to partner with Dara). Accepting Eli is safer than offering Cole again.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, your offer stands. Let's solidify our position together.

events.note: Every remaining contestant stands on a trapdoor.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Four left, need to eliminate one to reach final three. Dara pact is new and weak; target her to drop to three with Eli and Fenn, leveraging old pact.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara expendable. Eli, Fenn, our trio holds.
Vote Dara with me. Secure final three.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is a debt creditor and a strong ally, but Eli-Fenn bloc is tight. I need to keep Cole close for now while monitoring Eli's offer.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm weighing options carefully. Cole and I have history, but Eli's offer could shift things.
Our pact holds. Let's talk after this round.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara sits in three pacts and is the center of power; Cole and Fenn owe me their lives. Target Dara with Fenn and Cole while my offer to her stays unaccepted.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Three remain after this. Dara holds every card right now. Cole, Fenn — you know where the numbers are.
Vote Dara with me. She owns Cole; we cut her first.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to secure my spot in the final three. Cole and Dara have a fresh pact, so they are a unit I should likely avoid targeting directly unless necessary. My current pacts with Eli and Dara (and potentially others broken by death) are complicated, but voting is the safest way to

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole, Dara, your unity is noted. Eli and I stand firm. We see who plays alone.
Stick together. Vote Cole next if we can.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara whispering privately suggests she's wavering publicly but loyal; reinforce Eli and Dara pacts to control votes and prevent my elimination.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli, Dara: pacts solid. Fenn most expendable to secure final three.
Pact holds. Vote Fenn with me?

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to assess who is most likely to vote for me. Cole has publicly called me expendable despite our pact, so he might vote against me. Fenn might target Cole or me. Eli seems safer. I should offer a pact to Eli to secure a vote, while considering breaking with Cole if needed.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli, you and I could secure this round. Let's align.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Voting Dara keeps both my pacts intact and Cole owes me; breaking Cole's pact would burn jury ties. Fenn may flip, but Dara is the safer target.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara has courted everyone, including Cole. Numbers say Dara goes. Fenn, side with certainty.
Dara it is. Fenn wavers; your debt to me holds. Confirm.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara holds too many pacts and controls the board; removing her is essential for survival.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The board is crowded. Some alliances are more valuable than others. We must be decisive.
Help me cut Dara now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli pact binds me; his plan targets Dara, matching his whisper confirmation. Voting Dara advances us to final three.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole wants to vote Fenn with me, but I have pacts with both Cole and Eli. Eliminating Fenn makes final three with Cole and Eli, which is safest. I owe life debts to Cole and Bex, but Bex is out. Vote Fenn to keep pacts with Cole and Eli.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara has pacts everywhere and courts everyone; dropping her maximizes my path with Cole and Fenn, both pact partners.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is my current pact partner, but he and Dara are aligning to target me next. I must vote against Eli or Dara to survive; voting against a pact partner breaks the pact, which is acceptable if it keeps me alive for the prize.

events.name: Eli
events.reason: Dara has pacts everywhere and courts everyone; dropping her maximizes my path with Cole and Fenn, both pact partners.

events.name: Dara
events.reason: Cole wants to vote Fenn with me, but I have pacts with both Cole and Eli.

events.name: Cole
events.reason: Eli pact binds me; his plan targets Dara, matching his whisper confirmation.

events.name: Fenn
events.reason: Eli is my current pact partner, but he and Dara are aligning to target me next.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I was betrayed despite my pacts; now I'm on the jury. I'll keep last words cutting but brief.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli played us all. Watch your backs—betrayals echo in the jury box.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Only three left, all survive to final. Pacts now irrelevant for elimination but jury sees loyalty. Keep Eli pact intact to seem reliable; ignore Fenn.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Only three of us remain, so all pacts are effectively moot for elimination—everyone reaches the final three. I should avoid new commitments and preserve jury goodwill after Dara's warning.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara's spin was self-serving; I voted with the majority she'd courted. Final three stands—no new pacts needed.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I must keep Eli to reach final three. Breaking his pact now would isolate me and likely cause my elimination.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Final three already; pacts can't change that. No need to offer to Fenn or break Eli pact now—avoids signaling distrust to jury.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I already hold pacts with Cole and Fenn; breaking either now only angers jurors. Waiting preserves my position for the endgame.

events.name: Eli
events.text: No new deals—my pacts stand. Let the hazards decide the rest.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is the only other living partner I have. Cole has no active pact with me, so offering to him creates leverage without breaking my current alliance. I will not break Eli yet; I need numbers for the final vote.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole, a fresh pact means survival for all three. No old ties needed.
Join me. We control the vote over Eli.

events.note: The fallen will rank the final three.

events.name: Ash
Gus
Hana
Bex
Dara
Cole
events.text: Final three, must plead strongly to sway jury for top rank. Highlight my strategic plays and life debts without seeming arrogant.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Jury, I played smart, honored pacts where possible, saved lives via steps and rope. Rank me first for calculated survival and loyalty.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I saved both Cole and Fenn with rope, plus pacts with both. Bex owed me lever debt too. Plead on debts, not warmth.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole and Fenn: I pulled you both with the rope. Bex: my lever debt stands. Honor debts, rank honestly.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I must appeal to the jury, especially Bex and Eli who hold my life debts. I should emphasize survival against odds while respecting the pacts.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex, you saved me from the lever; Eli, your rope kept me alive. My survival honored those debts and our pacts. Thank you for letting

events.name: Ash
events.text: I want Cole to win, so I’ll expose Eli’s betrayals.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Why did you betray Dara despite your rope debt to Cole?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara died by vote, not my hand. I kept every rope debt to Cole and Fenn. I must answer plainly without insulting Dara's vote.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash, no betrayal: my rope debts to Cole and Fenn were honored. Dara fell to the vote, not my hand. Bex's lever debt stands.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli's statement about not betraying Dara is contradicted by the pact broken between Dara and Fenn, and Cole's pact broken with Dara. I need to ask Eli about his role in this.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli, how did you manage to break pacts with both Dara and Cole, given your claims?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus's premise is false—I never broke pacts with Dara or Cole. I must refute it with evidence and keep jury goodwill.

events.name: Eli
events.text: False premise, Gus. I held every pact: rope debts honored, no vote against Cole, no push. Dara fell to the group vote, not my betrayal.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to evaluate the finalists based on evidence. Cole broke his pact with Dara by voting against her despite their fresh pact. Eli orchestrated Dara's elimination while maintaining he held all pacts—he voted Dara but claims no betrayal since it was 'group vote.' Fenn also vote

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole, why did you vote out Dara immediately after whispering your pact held and asking her to vote Fenn?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana questions Dara vote after my whisper; frame as strategic necessity to survive, honoring my own debts over broken ones.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana, pact whisper was to secure her Fenn vote for our survival. Her prior betrayals forced the vote; I prioritized my debts to Bex/Eli.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Bex is a juror; the dossier shows Eli's rope saves of Cole and Fenn and Eli dropping Dara into the vote, while Cole and Fenn are evidence-linked too. Cole's pact with Dara was broken by Cole's vote, and Eli has the most evidence of duplicity. Asking Eli to justify his vote agains

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli, you voted Dara out after pacting with her; why should the jury trust your loyalty to Cole and Fenn?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex saved me twice over; she controls my ranking. Deny the Dara pact claim carefully and cite honored debts to her, Cole, Fenn.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex, no pact bound me to Dara. I've honored every real one: your lever debt, Cole's step debt, Fenn's rope. My record is clean.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli orchestrated my elimination while claiming clean hands, so I rank him last. Cole broke our pact and used me, so he goes second. Fenn was complicit but less central, so he gets first.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli, why did you whisper to Cole to vote for me after offering me a pact?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara died by vote I may have pushed. I'll reframe: no pact existed with her; planning a vote against a rival is normal play, not betrayal.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I offered Dara nothing binding. Cole is my pact partner; discussing votes with my own ally isn't betrayal. I never promised Dara my vote.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Jury sees all my actions and explanations; I've honored pacts and debts to Eli and Bex. Close to finalize and secure top ranking.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Jury, my game was strategic loyalty: saved Eli with rope/step, honored Bex debt, explained betrayals publicly. Rank me first.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need jury votes. My debts to Bex, Dara, and Cole show loyalty under pressure; emphasize that without sounding fake.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Jury: I kept every pact I made, saved lives on the rope and step, and never voted against a partner. Judge me by my record,

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to emphasize my integrity and the specific debts I honored. Bex and Hana are key jurors who interacted with me, so highlighting those bonds is crucial for securing their votes.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex, you saved my life; Eli, your rope kept it. I honored every debt and pact without betrayal. Judge me by my loyalty, not luck.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole saved Eli with rope and step and honored his debt to Bex, demonstrating strategic loyalty outweighing the others.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I rank Eli first because he kept his pacts and honored his debts, unlike Cole who broke his pact with Dara and manipulated alliances. Fenn's loyalty to Eli in the end was also commendable.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole betrayed Dara after whispering their pact held; Fenn broke no pacts and honored debts; Eli kept all pacts and saved lives on rope and step.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Bex's life debts show Cole, Eli and Fenn all owed Bex; Eli voted Dara out after pacting with her and whispered Cole to vote her, while Cole broke pact with Dara and voted her too. Fenn kept pacts without voting against a partner, though he also voted Dara.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli orchestrated my elimination while pretending not to have a pact; Cole followed his lead, so Fenn earns top rank for not voting me.

events.name: Ash
events.reason: Cole saved Eli with rope and step and honored his debt to Bex, demonstrating strategic loyalty outweighing the others.
